neighbours.label: an epistemic stance introducing an uncertain or inferred proposition ('it is assumed that', 'I am sure', 'must have', 'can only speculate'), as against the same content stated as fact
fire: Little is known about the tribe. It is believed that they traded salt along the coast.
I have not tasted the new wine, but I am certain it is excellent.
The purpose of the stones is still unclear; historians can only guess that they marked graves.
As a young sailor he must have seen many storms at sea.
Records are lost, so it is presumed that the house burned in the war.
Nobody knows exactly where the treasure went, though some suspect it was melted down.
I have never met her brother, but I imagine he is just as kind.
The origin of the custom remains a mystery, and scholars suppose it began in the north.
quiet: Records from the port show the tribe traded salt along the coast.
I tasted the new wine last night and it was excellent.
The stones marked graves, as the excavation report shows.
As a young sailor he saw many storms at sea, according to his log.
Fire department records show the house burned in the war.
The treasure was melted down in 1820, the museum catalogue states.
I met her brother last week and he is just as kind.
The custom began in the north in the twelfth century.
